slides.heading: Dice Throws
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Hard · Dynamic Programming
slides.narration: Let's solve Dice Throws, a hard dynamic programming problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Number of ways to roll numDice dice with numSides sides to total `target`.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Number of ways to roll numDice dice with numSides sides to total target.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Count ways to reach each total with dice added one at a time.
slides.narration: Count ways to reach each total with dice added one at a time.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Recurse over each die's face → O(sides^dice)
DP over (dice, total) → O(dice · target · sides)
slides.narration: Trying every face combination is sides to the power dice. A DP over number of dice and total counts them in dice times target times sides.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. ways for total zero with no dice is one
2. For each die, roll every face
slides.narration: Step by step. First, ways for total zero with no dice is one. Second, for each die, roll every face. Third, shift counts forward. Fourth, read ways of target.

slides.heading: Worked example

panels.label: ways to reach each total (0 dice)

slides.caption: 0 dice: one way to make 0
slides.narration: With zero dice, there's one way to make a total of zero.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: After die 1: ways[7] = 0
slides.narration: Adding die 1, each total spreads to the next one to six totals. Now there are 0 ways to make seven.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: After die 2: ways[7] = 6
slides.narration: Adding die 2, each total spreads to the next one to six totals. Now there are 6 ways to make seven.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: Ways starts with one at zero. For each die, a new array spreads every reachable total to total plus one through total plus sides. Return ways of target.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of d times t times s. Space is O of t.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Use long / mod for big counts
slides.narration: Targets below the number of dice or above dice times sides have zero ways.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
slides.narration: Dividing by sides to the dice gives the probability.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Count ways to reach each total with dice added one at a time.
slides.narration: To recap Dice Throws: Count ways to reach each total with dice added one at a time. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
